advantages.what: Keyboard Confirm/Reject moves focus to that proposal's Change result, so a second Enter cannot decide another proposal (X confirms or rejects a second proposal the person never chose)
Field names are case-insensitive; in X a capitalised field name silently creates a second field on the record

A storage write failure puts the app into a reported unavailable mode with a recovery step; X leaves a pending reply stuck and the conversation blocked, and a running task showing Running with no progress, until restart
Storage failure during a task step is reported rather than leaving the task silently Running
Saving under an existing name is refused with a message; X silently overwrites, and after a refused rename the form stays bound to the edited entry so the next new instruction replaces it
Duplicate-name save of instructions and tasks refused instead of silent overwrite
Conversations get distinct labels (Chat n, distinguishing excerpt) and same-named bots get a stable Bot #n
Same-named bots can be told apart before selecting
Damaged or unreadable data folder refuses start with a plain recovery message instead of a raw stack trace
ORD-1001A gets a notice that the identifier could not be used instead of ORD-1001's value
add step feedback names the task by number, so same-titled tasks are told apart
Invalid values (a word into total, unknown fields, inexact amounts) are refused with correction guidance before Confirm
Its tests catch DATA_DIR being ignored (S-5); X's suite stays green when DATA_DIR is ignored
Since you were away still reports finished and failed work when returning in a browser without the stored baseline
Saved instructions shows 'Active on <bot>: <text>', so the copied instruction the bot uses stays visible
Builder harness (acceptance/ scripts) and a cross-tier receipt protocol a maintainer must carry

lesser_lacks: Move focus after Confirm/Reject to that proposal's Change result instead of the next same-named button
Match record field names without regard to capitals in lookups and changes
Mark a pending reply failed and a running task Interrupted/Failed when progress cannot be saved, with a storage error the person can act on
Refuse saving an instruction or task under an existing name without Edit, and clear the edit binding after a refused rename
Give empty and similarly-opened conversations distinct labels, and make same-named bots distinguishable
Refuse to start on a damaged or unwritable data folder with a plain message and recovery step
Tell the person a suffixed id such as ORD-1001A cannot be found
Identify which of two same-titled tasks received an added step
Validate proposed values and say how to correct them
pairs.why: Both meet every stated requirement, but X carries ten more defects, two of them in the confirm path the request stresses: a second keyboard Enter decides a proposal the person did not choose, and a capitalised field name silently adds a field. X also hangs replies and tasks on storage failure and silently loses saved entries, while Y handles each of these; X's only real edges are the browser-independent away summary and the visible active instruction text. Closing that list takes several separate fixes across the client, records and storage layers, well over an hour.

pairs.why: Z avoids seven of X's defects, including the two in the confirm path (keyboard focus deciding another proposal, a capitalised field silently adding a field) and the stuck reply and task after a storage failure. X's edges over Z are small: a browser-independent away summary and showing the active instruction text. The fixes X needs reach the client focus handling, the records layer, storage error paths and startup, too much for one short task.

pairs.why: The two share the same core behaviour and handle storage failure, damaged data and the confirm flow equally well; Y adds a set of naming and identification fixes (conversation labels, bot numbers, task numbers in steer feedback, suffixed ids) and friendlier record-request handling. Each gap in Z is a small, local labelling or parsing change, so one short follow-up would close them. Y carries somewhat more code and shipped harness for a maintainer, which tempers the margin.
